neighbours.label: the likelihood predicate ' likely' / ' unlikely' (very likely, not likely to, is unlikely), as opposed to the same sentences stating or hedging the outcome without a likelihood word
fire: With these clouds, more rain is likely by the evening.
Experts say a full recovery is unlikely before next year.
The new rules are likely to raise prices for small shops.
Without water, the young trees are unlikely to survive the summer.
Given his injury, the striker is not likely to play on Saturday.
Delays at the border are very likely during the holiday weekend.
A deal between the two parties now seems unlikely.
If the dam fails, flooding downstream is highly likely.
quiet: With these clouds, more rain may come by the evening.
Experts say a full recovery will take until next year.
The new rules will raise prices for small shops.
Without water, the young trees will die in the summer.
Given his injury, the striker will rest on Saturday.
Delays at the border happen during the holiday weekend.
A deal between the two parties now looks lovely on paper.
If the dam fails, the valley downstream will flood.

predictions: likely/unlikely items 0.75-0.97; matched sentences with may/will or look-alike words below 0.15
